title: Customer Services
summary: 'Customer is boss' – the success and revenue of a product or service depend on customer acceptance and satisfaction. The customer service representative is the face of the business: the first impression is the last impression, so keeping customers happy and retaining them is a demanding skill.

Greet with a smile (a customer left unattended may go to another store; a welcome and smile make the customer feel valued). Offer help ('May I help you?') and inform about product qualities instead of telling the customer what to buy. Pay undivided attention: stop other work and attend to the customer first, or politely guide the customer to the right person. Be formal: converse formally and professionally; over-friendly behaviour may cause trouble. Dress professionally: neat, groomed, hair combed; a decent appearance makes customers interact confidently.

Customers can reach a business by direct contact, mobile phone, SMS, e-mail and real-time chat, so communication must be effective. Points: greet customers and verify their details (registered phone number, name); be an active listener (focus, positive body language, eye contact, nod, take notes; on the phone use phrases like 'Ok, yes I understand'); impress by repeating your understanding and seeking the customer's approval; never interrupt; use clear words and sentences (say 'Is the computer starting?' instead of 'booting'); be formal and avoid jargon and acronyms such as ASAP and FYI even in electronic communication; be courteous ('Sir/Madam, can I have the serial id?'); always appear ready to help and use positive statements instead of 'I will not be able to help you'; be cautious of words that cause unexpected reactions (say 'Kindly excuse, I am unable to hear you clearly'); check background noise and distractions; take into account the customer's preferred mode of communication (e-mail or message); seek support from colleagues and team members when stuck.

Courteous handling of an issue retains customers whereas an indifferent 'I don't know' attitude loses them and invites negative publicity; calls are recorded for quality checks; respond immediately to e-mails and calls. Follow up until the issue is resolved: schedule appointments, take feedback, transfer to a skilled technician in another department. The representative must have complete knowledge of the product and service and the latest, accurate company policies, strong communication skills, and on the phone speak slowly, stay patient and calm even if the customer is upset, listen to the complaint first and then ask small, crisp, minimum questions.
q1: What should be your first step to make a customer happy?
Greet the customer with a smile and a welcome message.
October 2025
Why should short forms of words or sentences not be used while communicating with a customer?
Jargon and acronyms such as ASAP or FYI may not be understood by the customer, so clear words should be used.
October 2025
State true or false: You can use jargons while interacting with a customer.
False.
October 2024
State true or false: Always greet your customer with a smile.
True.
October 2024
Who is the 'face of the business'?
The customer service representative.
Why should you be formal even if the customer is friendly?
To keep a uniform, professional interaction; over-friendly behaviour may land you in trouble.
How should you dress while dealing with customers?
Formally, neat and well groomed.
What is an active listener?
One who focuses on what the customer says, uses positive body language and acknowledges before replying.
What should you do if you cannot hear the customer clearly on the phone?
Politely say 'Kindly excuse, I am unable to hear you clearly' instead of asking them to speak clearly.
Why should you never interrupt a customer?
Interruption is taken as an offence and may upset the customer.
Name one way of seeking support while serving a customer.
Take help of colleagues or team members.
q2: Explain the main points to deliver excellent customer service.

Greet with a smile and offer help; give undivided attention; be courteous and formal; listen actively and never interrupt; use clear words; resolve and follow up until the issue is solved; know the product and company policy.
April 2026
(i) What is the importance of seeking support while dealing with customers? (ii) Why should you be formal while communicating with your customers?

(i) Colleagues may know a solution and each has a unique way of handling queries, so support helps resolve the issue. (ii) Formal language keeps interaction professional and avoids misunderstanding or trouble.
April 2025
(i) Why is giving undivided attention necessary for customer satisfaction? (ii) Why is it necessary to be dressed professionally?
(i) The customer feels valued and the query is solved quickly. (ii) A neat, decent appearance lets customers interact confidently and freely.
April 2024
What qualities are expected from a customer service representative?
Politeness, active listening, clear communication, knowledge of product and policies, patience and calm behaviour, ability to resolve problems.
October 2024
Why is it important to dress well as a customer representative?
A decent and groomed appearance creates a good first impression and gives customers confidence.
Why should you not be over-friendly with the customer?
It may land you in trouble and affect uniformity and professionalism in interaction.
List the basic communication skills required while interacting with the customer.
Active listening, not interrupting, clear words, courtesy, formal tone, positive statements, noting the preferred mode of communication.
Why is it important to know the company policies as a customer service representative?
To resolve conflicts and answer queries correctly using latest, accurate information.
Write a polite way to ask for a product's serial id.
'Sir/Madam, can I have the serial id of the product?'
Why should the representative follow up with the customer?
To ensure the complete resolution of the problem, which gives a satisfied customer and good word of mouth.
What is meant by 'Pay undivided attention'?
Stopping all other work and attending to the customer's query first or guiding them politely to the right person.
Why should you take notes and repeat what you understood?
To confirm the customer's requirement and seek approval, showing that you listened.
q3: Explain how to greet a customer.
Greet with a smile and welcome message, offer help without pressing what to buy, give undivided attention, remain formal and dress professionally.
Explain any three basic communication points with a customer.
Be an active listener with eye contact and notes; use clear words without jargon; be courteous and positive, e.g. 'Sir/Madam, can I have the serial id?' instead of commanding.
Assume you are at an IT helpdesk and a customer is annoyed since the engineer has not called. How will you resolve it?
Greet and apologise politely, verify the complaint number and details, listen without interrupting, assure follow-up, contact the engineer or department, give a time, and follow up until solved.
Explain the key to excellent customer service.
Courteous handling and immediate response retain customers; follow up until resolution; know the product and policies; speak slowly and calmly; keep questions short.
Explain how to handle situations of noise, preferred mode of communication and seeking support.
Move to a quiet place when on the phone; ask for the customer's preferred mode (e-mail or message); seek help from colleagues when stuck and learn from them.
Why are words and phrases important when talking to customers? Give examples.
Right words keep the customer positive: say 'Kindly excuse, I am unable to hear you clearly' rather than 'Speak clearly'; use 'Is the computer starting?' instead of 'booting'.
